basis: Absent or dystrophic nails and congenital digit malformations define the syndrome.
Growth hormone-secreting neoplasm originates in the anterior pituitary; secondary endocrine syndromes do not establish additional organ labels.
Papillary urothelial carcinoma arises in the bladder or renal pelvis; both belong to the renal axis.
Carcinoma in situ is located in the liver.
Mitochondrial disorder with defining neurologic and ocular dysfunction; myopathy occurs in 30-79%. Hepatic failure excluded because it is commonly valproate-associated.
Developmental impairment characterizes symptomatic 16q duplications; congenital heart defects occur in roughly half of reported cases, varying with duplicated segment.
Intestinal atresia and volvulus define gastrointestinal involvement; absence of the superior mesenteric artery is a defining vascular malformation.
Developmental disability and brain malformations define ZTTK; strabismus 55%, hypermetropia and joint hypermobility 30-79%. Genitourinary annotations do not establish renal frequency.
The tumour originates in the placenta, an obstetric organ outside the axes; a vascular subtype does not define the entire umbrella.
Defective glycosylation is metabolic; neurodevelopmental dysfunction affects most patients, and coagulation-factor deficiencies commonly exceed 30%. Other organ damage varies by subtype.
